label: text

POSITION OF GERMAN
TRADE.

label: text
text: DYERS REVIEW

label: text
text:
Berlin, September 3.
The general depression in German industries and their inability to meet their increasing demands for raw materials unless there is a considerable expansion in export trade was emphasised by Herr Duisberg, Chairman of the Association of German Industriallsts and Chairman of the German dye industry, in speech at a general meeting of the Association at Dresden.

label: text
text: Herr Duisberg, who has just returned from a world tour, finds the position in the country generally worse than when he left Germany. He said that the engineering industry was in a worse position in July than in June. The position of the iron and steel industry was extremely bad, as was evidenced by the number of unemployed, whilst the dyestuff industry, which was the backbone of the chemical industry, was very unsatisfactory, the business being under 50 per cent. of the average turnover.

label: text
text: Hierro Duisberg accused America of dumping competition. He said that although the export from the mining and iron industry had rather improved as the result of the British miners' strike the home demand for coal remained very unsatisfactory.

label: text
text:
Herr Duisberg said that he expected the impending conclusion of the iron and steel impact to bring to an end French and Belgian dumping sales in South Germany.
The position of the electro-technical industry was generally satisfactory, but paper and textiles were not prospering with the exception of artificial silk, velvet, and silk. He concluded by recommending the strictest economy and an all round reduction it imports to the minimum.—Reuter.

label: text
text: MINERS' REQUEST TO CHANCELLOR

label: text
text: FRESH NEGOTIATIONS.

label: text
text: A letter addressed to the Chancellor of the Exchequer, signed by Mr. A. J. Cook, states that the Miners' Executive and the delegate conference request the Chancellor to convene and attend a conference of the Mining Association and the Miners' Federation. The latter are prepared to negotiate a new national agreement with a view to reducing labour costs to meet the immediate necessities of the industry.

label: text
text: Following receipt of the letter from the Executive of the Miners' Federation the Government has requested the Mining Association to resume negotiations.—Reuter.

label: text
text: The Miners' Executive, in consultation with Mr. Ramsay MacDonald and other members of the Parliamentary Labour Party, have spent most of the day in discussing and drafting proposals with a view to reopening the coal negotiations. It is stated that good progress was made.

label: text
text: When completed the proposals will be submitted to the Government, who will then decide whether they offer a basis for fruitful negotiations. If, as is hoped, the proposals show a definite advance the Government will invite the mine owners to resume negotiations and to display reciproce concessions.

label: text
text: Mr. Churchill, who will be responsible for any action taken by the Government during the Prime Minister's absence abroad, and the Labour and Mines Ministers are remaining in London during the week-end to deal with developments.

label: text
text: The Miners' Executive will probably approach the Government to-morrow. — British Wireless Service.

label: paragraph_title

label: text
text: OBJECTIONABLE PROPOSAL

label: text
text: The Council this afternoon debated a report by M. Unden (Sweden) on the work of the Mandates Commission.

label: text
text: At the June session M. Briand (France), General Smuts (South Africa) Count Isali (Japan) Sir John Bell (New Zealand) and others agreed with Sir Austen Chamberlain, who strongly objected to the proposal of the Commission to address a questionnaire to the Mandatory Powers dealing with the administration of the mandated territories and the Commission to hear verbal petitions from the inhabitants of the Mandated territories.

label: text
text: Sir Austen Chamberlain stigmatised such a questionnaire as inquisitorial and opposed the commission's hearing of verbal petitions without first hearing the Mandatory observations thereanent.

label: text
text:
The general opinion of the Council was that the Mandates Commission has exceeding its powers as regards supervising the administration of the mandated territories.—

Reuter.

text: His Excellency the Governor in Council has ordered, under section 2 of the Rating (Refunds) Ordinance, 1926, Ordinance No. 3 of 1926, that refund of rates for the third quarter of the year 1926 be as where, after the two-two floor there are to have been vacant during the whole of any month in the said quarter: Such refund will not be of the whole of the rates attributable to such vacant floors but will be made having regard to the allowance in the assessment for partial vacancy: No refund of rates for the said quarter will be made in any case where such rates have not been paid in advance as required by the Rating Ordinance, 1901.

text: The concession intimated in Government Notification No. 96 of 192 is confirmed as regards refunds in respect of the months of February and March, and the second quarter of the year 1926; but no concession under such notification or under this order is to be claimed or expected in respect of any period after the third quarter of 1926.
